You are working on Resurgo's web app on the `web` branch in this worktree. Read web/NOTES.md, docs/LANDING.md and docs/ANIMATION.md first. Keep changes small and commit in small steps.

1. **Use logos instead of product names, the way checklyhq.com does.** The official logo files are already in `web/public/logos/` (uncommitted). `web/public/logos/SOURCES.md` lists where each came from and how each may be coloured. Commit them.
   - What Checkly does, measured on their site today:
     - A small uppercase label with wide tracking, such as "WORKS WITH" at about 12px and 0.12em letter-spacing.
     - Then a row of logos in place of the names, about 14 to 16px tall, with 16px gaps.
     - Colourful logos keep their brand colour. Black-and-white logos are drawn in one colour that suits the theme.
     - Integration grids use 24px icons.
   - Replace names with logos in these places:
     - **The stack strip**, the `names = ["Node", "pnpm", "npm", "Yarn", "Foundry", "Cargo", "Docker", "GitHub"]` list in pages/Landing.tsx. Show one logo per tool, with Cargo shown as the Rust logo. Don't add tools Resurgo doesn't support today. Bun arrives with agent v2, so leave it out for now but keep its file.
     - **The "Built on neatlogs tracing and Entire checkpoints" line.** Put the neatlogs wordmark and the Entire logo inline, sized to the text and aligned on the baseline. Don't add cfo.ai until the business plan exists, but keep its file.
     - **The "Install on GitHub" buttons.** Put the GitHub mark before the label.
   - Monochrome logos (neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai, Foundry, GitHub, Rust, Bun) must follow the theme, so render them in `currentColor`. Use a CSS mask for the raster files (`neatlogs-wordmark.webp`, `foundry-mark.png`), and inline SVG or a mask for the SVGs.
   - Colour logos (Node, pnpm, npm, Yarn, Docker) use the brand colours listed in SOURCES.md, in both themes.
   - Accessibility:
     - Every logo carries the product name, as `alt` or as `role="img"` with `aria-label`.
     - A logo that replaces a word in a sentence must still read as that word to a screen reader.
     - Add a `title` tooltip with the name.
   - One small `Logo` component is enough. Add no new library.
2. **Fix copy that is no longer true.** The GitHub App, "Resurgo Agent", now exists and opens pull requests for verified fixes.
   - Update every place that says the App isn't built yet or is "planned": the closing section ("the next thing to build"), the chat reply, the "Planned flow" label, and the agent-view text in `api/main.py`.
   - Say only what is true. You install it on the repos you pick. It opens a pull request only for a fix that passed in a clean container. Code changes wait for your approval.
   - Don't promise schedules or anything else that isn't built.
3. **Add a third status for code fixes.** Agent v2 will produce records where the fix passed in the clean container but changes code, so it waits for the owner's approval. In those records `verifier.passed` is true and `needs_approval` is true.
   - Today `_verified` in `api/main.py` would show these as "Runs · verified clean".
   - Add a distinct status for them, "Fix verified · awaiting approval", in the API summary, the gallery and the run view. Style it so it can't be mistaken for a clean pass.
   - A record with `needs_approval` true and a failed or missing verifier stays "Broken", as it is today.
4. **Check your work.**
   - Run `npm run build`, then `web/check-render.mjs` at 420 and 1280px, in light and dark.
   - Extend the check so it also confirms two things: the stack strip and the "Built on" line render logos with accessible names, and nothing overflows at 420px.
   - Take close-up screenshots of the logo strip and the "Built on" line in both themes, and look at them yourself. Every logo must be visible, crisp and evenly sized.

Rules:
- Don't push, don't merge, and don't edit hackathon.md.
- Never read `.env` or `.entire/settings.local.json`.
- Run no `docker` commands.
- Never print secrets or server addresses.
- No tool or AI attribution in commits.
- Finish with a short report: what changed, the check results with screenshot paths, and anything you weren't sure about.
I'll start by reading the three docs and the logos' SOURCES.md.

31	## Interaction and motion: what checklyhq.com actually does (studied hands-on 10 Oct)
32	
33	How their page works. These are observations, not code to copy:
34	
35	- **Everything is live HTML/SVG in React.** There are no videos, canvases or Lottie files, and the product panels are DOM rebuilds rather than screenshots. That keeps them crisp at any size and easy to theme.
36	- **The hero is a choreographed story** of about 8 seconds: user prompt, agent plan, `Write(file)` with code, terminal `test` (✓ 4s, 1 passed), `deploy` (✓ 4 locations), then live status tiles. Windows enter with a 0.6 s rise, staggered. Lines are already in the DOM and fade in (0.2 s for chat, 0.35 s for code).
37	- **Agent replies stream character by character** at about 30–40 characters per second, with short pauses between paragraphs and a cursor.
38	- **Interactive but scripted.** The chat box accepts any text. Sending posts your bubble, then a canned reply streams in, and the dashboard beside it reacts: a counter goes up by one and a new row appears marked "just now". It feels real because the whole UI responds to your input.
39	- **Tabs advance on their own.** Each tab swaps the headline, three stat cards and a fresh streamed conversation.
40	- **Sub-views:** product panels toggle between "App UI" and "Code", showing the output next to the code behind it.
41	- **Ambient liveness:** location tiles cycle between PASS and FAIL every few seconds, the integration cards scroll in a marquee, and the closing strip's bars grow red to amber to green on scroll, in step with a four-step timeline.
42	- **Small details:** a copy-command chip, an "Agent view" link to a machine-readable page (`/index.md`), muted translucent text, and a plain monospace stack.
43	- **Some parts are decorative:** the dashboard's pagination does nothing.

45	## How Resurgo applies it, with real data instead of a script
46	
47	- **Hero story (about 10 s), replaying the REAL rinne run:** a project row "rinne · ✗ Broken from fresh clone"; the agent window streams the real diagnosis; fixes 1 and 2 fail and fix 3 passes, each with its real error and timing; the terminal window shows `pnpm install` ✗ to ✓; clean-container tiles show clone, toolchain and install ✓; the verdict is "✓ Runs".
48	- **Live tiles:** gallery repos with their REAL latest statuses, cycling on the same kind of timer as Checkly's location tiles. Broken repos stay broken; no status is faked.
49	- **Chat box:** "Paste a public GitHub repo". If the repo is in the gallery, its real run replays with streaming. Otherwise, say plainly that live checks come with the GitHub App, or queue a real check if the runner is opened to visitors (stretch goal). Never stream an invented result.
50	- **Solution tabs that advance on their own:** Check, Diagnose, Repair, Prove. Each tab shows a real streamed excerpt and real stat cards, and hides any stat that isn't measured yet.
51	- **Sub-view toggles:** "Run" and "Fix diff" on run panels, showing the result next to the patch.
52	- **Closing strip:** bars from real sweep results, v1 then v2, so any red-to-green movement is real.
53	- **Agent view:** a `/index.md`, with an `llms.txt`, describing Resurgo and its API for agents.
54	- **Motion:** 0.6 s staggered window rises, 0.2–0.35 s line fades, streaming at about 35 characters per second, ambient loops of 3–5 s, and `prefers-reduced-motion` showing final states.

1	# Motion checklist: Lasseter's principles applied to Resurgo
2	
3	Source: John Lasseter, "Principles of Traditional Animation Applied to 3D Computer Animation", SIGGRAPH 1987. PDF: https://www.ics.uci.edu/~fowlkes/class/ics162/exercises/lasseter.pdf (mirror: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/academic/class/15462-f13/www/lec_slides/Lesseter.pdf)
4	
5	**Rule for every animator (Claude, Codex, Agy):** read the paper and this list before animating anything. Afterwards, report one line per principle: what you did and where.
6	
7	1. **Squash and stretch.** Use subtle scale changes that preserve volume, only at moments of contact. Buttons compress to about 0.97 on press and settle back. The verdict chip lands with a single overshoot to about 1.03. Never squash text.
8	2. **Timing.** Duration conveys weight. Chips take 120–180 ms and windows 450–650 ms. Reading pauses scale with text length, roughly 250 ms plus 30 ms per word, so the eye can finish before the next beat. Streaming runs at about 35 characters per second. Real durations always appear as labels, even when time is compressed.
9	3. **Anticipation.** Cue each beat before it happens. The cursor blinks twice before typing starts. A window's title bar appears about 120 ms before its body. The spinner appears before output streams. A tab's indicator moves before its content swaps.
10	4. **Staging.** Run one focal action at a time. Dim inactive windows to about 0.55 opacity while another one acts. The eye path is project row, agent, terminal, clean container, verdict. Never animate the main content of two windows at once.
11	5. **Follow-through and overlapping action.** Children trail their parents: a window's content staggers 30–60 ms behind its frame. Lines settle with a 2 px overshoot. After the verdict lands, the tile row finishes moving a moment later.
12	6. **Straight-ahead versus pose-to-pose.** The story is pose-to-pose: key beats taken from the real run record (idle, failing, fixing, proving, verdict), planned first. Streaming text, timers and spinners are straight-ahead, generated as they play.
13	7. **Slow in and slow out.** Entrances share one easing, for example `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`, and exits use a gentler one. Nothing moves linearly except timers, progress and spinner rotation.
14	8. **Arcs.** Moving elements travel on slight curves (X and Y with different easings), not straight diagonals. The orb drifts on an arc.
15	9. **Exaggeration.** Push only the key moments. The failing ✗ line flashes red once for 300 ms, the winning fix line gets one quick lemon sweep, and the verdict alone gets a scale overshoot. Everything else stays calm.
16	10. **Secondary action.** It supports the main action and never competes with it. The orb breathes only while the model is thinking, the cursor blinks, timers tick, and tile status dots pulse softly. All of these pause when the primary action needs attention.
17	11. **Appeal.** Aim for clarity and personality: legible type, generous spacing, honest data and a steady rhythm. The agent should feel calm and competent, with one small flourish at the win: the lifted-r mark gives a short "lift" when a run verifies.
18	
19	Also:
20	- `prefers-reduced-motion` shows final poses only.
21	- Motion is never the only signal. Every state is a word plus a glyph.
22	- Every replay comes from a real run record. Animation never invents a result.
23	
24	## Video output quality (standing rule)
25	- Every video has a **4K master: 3840x2160**. Render web content at a 1920x1080 layout with deviceScaleFactor 2 so text stays crisp. Encode H.264 High at CRF 16 or better, yuv420p. Use 60 fps for motion-heavy pieces (30 fps is acceptable for slow ones).

236	_HOW = """## How a run is proved
237	
238	1. **Fresh clone.** The agent container clones the repository at a pinned commit, picks the package manager from the lockfile, and runs install, build, test and start in order, stopping at the first failure.
239	2. **Diagnose.** Deterministic rules run first. A model is called only when a step failed; it proposes the least invasive fix (configuration before source code).
240	3. **Repair.** The fix is applied as a patch and the failed step is run again. Source-code changes are proposed and marked `needs_approval`; they are not applied on their own.
241	4. **Prove.** A second, separate container rebuilds from a fresh clone with the recipe and the patch only. Its steps are recorded as `verifier.steps`. The agent that wrote the fix cannot write to it.
242	
243	## Status vocabulary
244	
245	- `runs` (✓ Runs): the verifier ran and every step passed.
246	- `runs_with_gaps` (◐ Runs with gaps): the verifier passed, and the record lists `gaps` (things it could not exercise, such as a missing test script).
247	- `broken` (✗ Broken): a step failed and no verified fix exists.
248	- `checking` (◌ Checking): the run has started and has no record yet.
249	- `fixed` (◐ Fixed, unverified): only in records from an earlier agent version that have no verifier steps at all.
250	
251	A run counts as verified only when `verified` is true: the verifier has at least one step and all steps exited 0. Nothing is claimed beyond the recorded steps; for example a verifier that only ran `install` has proved the install, not the build.
